6. Use principles of molecular structure, intermolecular forces, and kinetic molecular theory to answer the
   following questions.

    (a) A complete Lewis electron-dot diagram of a molecule of ethyl methanoate is given below.





            (i) Identify the hybridization of the valence electrons of the carbon atom labeled Cw .

           (ii) Estimate the numerical value of the H y C x O bond angle in an ethyl methanoate molecule.
            Explain the basis of your estimate.

   (b) Ethyl methanoate, CH3CH2OCHO, is synthesized in the laboratory from ethanol, C2H5OH, and methanoic
        acid, HCOOH , as represented by the following equation.

                      Æ                                           CH3CH2OCHO(l) + H2O(l)                       C2H5OH(l) + HCOOH(l) ¨

            (i) In the box below, draw the complete Lewis electron-dot diagram of a methanoic acid molecule.





                                          Methanoic Acid

candidates.name: Molecular geometry (VSEPR)
candidates.definition: Predicting electron-domain geometry and molecular shape from the arrangement of bonding and lone-pair domains around a central atom.
candidates.include: Tag when a molecular or electron-domain geometry must be named, identified, drawn or used.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag hybridization-only questions (tag hybridization) or bond-angle questions where shape is given (tag bond-angles).

candidates.name: Electron-domain counting
candidates.definition: Counting the electron domains around a central atom, where each lone pair and each bond (single, double or triple) counts as one domain.
candidates.include: Tag when the answer depends on counting domains, including the rule that a multiple bond is one domain, as a supporting step for geometry or hybridization.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag when geometry or hybridization is simply recalled for a familiar molecule without domain reasoning being needed.

candidates.name: Intermolecular forces and physical properties
candidates.definition: Using the relative strength of intermolecular forces to explain or rank boiling point, melting point, vapor pressure, viscosity, surface tension or enthalpy of vaporization, and distinguishing intermolecular from intramolecular forces.
candidates.include: Tag when a physical property must be compared or explained in terms of intermolecular attractions; pair with the specific force concept(s) that decide the comparison.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag chemical reactivity or bond-breaking explanations; boiling does not break covalent bonds.

candidates.name: Bond angles
candidates.definition: Predicting or comparing bond angles from electron-domain geometry, including the compression caused by lone pairs.
candidates.include: Tag when a bond angle must be estimated, compared or explained.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag when only a shape name is requested.

candidates.name: Dipole-dipole attractions
candidates.definition: Attractions between the permanent dipoles of polar molecules.
candidates.include: Tag when dipole-dipole forces must be identified or compared.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag hydrogen bonding cases unless the comparison involves dipole-dipole forces specifically.

candidates.name: Molecular polarity
candidates.definition: Deciding whether a molecule has a net dipole from its bond dipoles and three-dimensional shape.
candidates.include: Tag when the student must determine or justify whether a molecule is polar or nonpolar.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag when polarity is stated in the question and only used to compare forces (tag the specific force).

candidates.name: Orbital hybridization
candidates.definition: Assigning sp, sp2 or sp3 hybridization to an atom from its number of electron domains.
candidates.include: Tag when the hybridization of an atom must be stated or used.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag geometry-only answers; d-orbital hybridization, drawing hybrid orbitals and molecular-orbital diagrams are not assessed.

candidates.name: Lewis structures
candidates.definition: Drawing or interpreting Lewis electron-dot diagrams: counting total valence electrons, placing bonding and lone pairs, multiple bonds, octet exceptions and polyatomic-ion charges.
candidates.include: Tag when the student must draw a Lewis structure, or must determine bonding and lone pairs that are not shown in order to answer.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag when a complete Lewis structure is given and is only read for a later step that is tagged separately, unless reading it requires electron counting.

candidates.name: Hydrogen bonding
candidates.definition: The strong dipole attraction between an H atom bonded to N, O or F and a lone pair on a nearby N, O or F atom.
candidates.include: Tag when hydrogen bonding must be identified, drawn, or used to explain a property, including identifying donors and acceptors.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag molecules that contain H and O but no H bonded to N, O or F (a common error).

candidates.name: London dispersion forces
candidates.definition: Attractions arising from temporary dipoles, whose strength increases with the number of electrons (polarizability) and with contact surface area.
candidates.include: Tag when dispersion forces must be identified or compared, especially using polarizability or molecular shape.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag merely because dispersion forces exist in every substance; tag only when they matter to the answer.

candidates.name: Collision model and temperature effects
candidates.definition: Explaining rate changes through collision frequency, the fraction of collisions with energy at least Ea (Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution), and correct orientation.
candidates.include: Tag when a change in rate with temperature, concentration or orientation must be explained at the particle level.
candidates.exclude: Numerical Arrhenius-equation calculations are not assessed.

candidates.name: Kinetic molecular theory
candidates.definition: Explaining gas behavior from particle motion: average kinetic energy proportional to absolute temperature, speed depending on molar mass, Maxwell-Boltzmann distributions, and pressure from collisions.
candidates.include: Tag when particle speed, kinetic energy, collision frequency or a speed distribution must be compared or explained.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag numerical ideal-gas calculations with no particle-level reasoning; numerical Graham's-law calculations are not assessed.

candidates.name: Oxidation numbers
candidates.definition: Assigning oxidation numbers to atoms and using changes in oxidation number to identify which species are oxidized and reduced and how many electrons transfer.
candidates.include: Tag when oxidation numbers must be assigned or changes in them used.
candidates.exclude: Terms 'oxidizing agent' and 'reducing agent' are not assessed on the current exam; do not confuse with formal charge.

candidates.name: Precipitation reactions
candidates.definition: Predicting whether a precipitate forms when solutions are mixed, using the AP-specified solubility facts (all sodium, potassium, ammonium and nitrate salts are soluble) and given data.
candidates.include: Tag when the student must predict or identify a precipitate qualitatively.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag quantitative Q versus Ksp precipitation tests (tag solubility-product); rote solubility rules beyond the AP-specified cases are not assessed.

candidates.name: Classifying reactions
candidates.definition: Recognizing acid-base, redox (including combustion) and precipitation reactions from equations or observations.
candidates.include: Tag when a reaction must be classified by type or its type is the key to predicting products.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag when the type is stated and the question asks only for a calculation.

candidates.name: Sigma and pi bonds
candidates.definition: Counting sigma and pi bonds in single, double and triple bonds and explaining restricted rotation about double bonds.
candidates.include: Tag when sigma and pi bonds must be counted or distinguished, or rotation about a bond is explained.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag simple bond-order comparisons (tag bond-order).

candidates.name: Ion-dipole attractions
candidates.definition: Attractions between ions and polar molecules, such as the orientation of water molecules around dissolved ions.
candidates.include: Tag when ion-dipole forces or hydration-shell orientation must be identified, drawn or used.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag ionic bonding within a lattice (tag lattice-energy).

candidates.name: Ion charges and ionic formulas
candidates.definition: Predicting common ion charges from valence electrons and periodic position, and writing charge-neutral ionic formulas.
candidates.include: Tag when the student predicts an ion's charge, the formula of an ionic compound, or explains ion formation from electron configuration.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag routine use of a given ionic formula in a calculation.

candidates.name: Solubility and 'like dissolves like'
candidates.definition: Predicting and explaining solubility and miscibility from the relative strength of solute-solute, solvent-solvent and solute-solvent attractions.
candidates.include: Tag when solubility or miscibility must be predicted or explained from molecular structure and forces.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag Ksp calculations (tag solubility-product) or solubility rules for precipitates (tag precipitation).

candidates.name: Bond polarity and partial charges
candidates.definition: Using electronegativity difference to decide whether a bond is polar, the direction of its dipole, and which atom carries the partial negative charge.
candidates.include: Tag when bond dipoles or partial charges on bonded atoms must be identified or compared.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag whole-molecule polarity questions unless individual bond dipoles are explicitly reasoned about (tag molecular-polarity).

candidates.name: Formal charge
candidates.definition: Calculating the formal charge on atoms in a Lewis structure and using formal charges to judge which of several structures best represents a species.
candidates.include: Tag when formal charges must be calculated, compared, or used to choose the preferred structure, even if the words 'formal charge' do not appear.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag oxidation numbers (tag oxidation-numbers) or a Lewis structure question whose answer does not depend on formal charge.

candidates.name: Bond order, length and strength
candidates.definition: Relating the number of shared electron pairs between two atoms (including fractional bond orders from resonance) to bond length and bond strength.
candidates.include: Tag when bond lengths or bond strengths are compared or explained from single, double, triple or resonance-averaged bonds.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag when bonds are only counted for a bond-enthalpy calculation (tag bond-enthalpy).

candidates.name: Net ionic equations
candidates.definition: Writing complete and net ionic equations by dissociating strong electrolytes and removing spectator ions, conserving atoms and charge.
candidates.include: Tag when a net ionic equation must be written or chosen, or spectator ions identified.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag when the reaction is only described in words and no ionic representation is required.

candidates.name: Energy of phase changes
candidates.definition: Heat absorbed or released during melting, vaporization, freezing and condensation (q = nΔH), constant temperature during a phase change, and heating or cooling curves.
candidates.include: Tag when enthalpies of fusion or vaporization, heating curves, or phase-change energy must be used.
candidates.exclude: Phase diagrams are not assessed.
